Tracts II and III have a total watershed area of approximately 25 and 23 mi<sup>2</sup>, respectively. Of this amount, about 40.5 mi<sup>2</sup> of Tracts II and III lie in Sarpy Creek basin. Thus, assuming all other factors being equal (e.g., soil type, terrain, vegetative cover, land use, climate, etc.) and that the worst possible effect of mining will result in a reduction in runoff from Tracts II and III of 50 percent, the net expected reduction in streamflow at the confluence of East Fork Sarpy Creek and Sarpy Creek is only about 13 percent and at the mouth of Sarpy Creek is only about 4.5 percent. Similarly, Tullock Creek would show only about a 1 percent reduction. Ground Water - Surface mining activities will penetrate the shallow ground-water system to the base of the Robinson coal. As a consequence, potentiometric surface and gradients in the ground-water flow system will be altered in the reclaimed mined area and somewhat altered in adjacent areas. This will result in modifying the direction and quantity of ground-water flow, and cause some relocation of discharge areas.
The Rosebud-McKay, the interburden, and the Robinson Coals each have a separate ground-water system. The Rosebud-McKay Coal near its clinker zones and in structural high areas is commonly drained so that the removal of that aquifer in the mined area will have minimal impact.
Surface mining activities as planned for Tracts II and III will result in forming a largely uniform "reclaimed aquifer" of spoils material from the land surface to the present position of the bottom of the Robinson Coal.
